title: Comparing and Ordering Three-Digit Numbers
introduction: Build on Primary 1 knowledge and practise comparing and ordering three-digit numbers.
definition: Compare hundreds first. If they are equal, compare tens; if those are equal, compare ones. Ascending order goes from smallest to largest, and descending order reverses it.

examples.question: Compare 582 and 528.
steps: Eight tens are greater than two tens.

exercises.question: Which is greater: 738 or 783?
exercises.solution: Both have 7 hundreds; 8 tens > 3 tens, so 783 > 738.

exercises.question: Which is smaller: 609 or 690?
exercises.solution: Both have 6 hundreds; 0 tens < 9 tens, so 609 < 690.

exercises.question: Write >, < or = : 412 __ 421
exercises.solution: Both have 4 hundreds; 1 ten < 2 tens, so 412 < 421.

exercises.question: Write >, < or = : 900 __ 899
exercises.solution: 900 has 9 hundreds and 899 has 8 hundreds, so 900 > 899.

exercises.question: Which is the largest of 321, 123 and 312?
exercises.solution: 321 and 312 have 3 hundreds; 321 has more tens. 321 > 312 > 123.

exercises.question: Which is the smallest of 509, 590 and 905?
exercises.solution: 509 and 590 have 5 hundreds; 509 has fewer tens. 509 < 590 < 905.

summary: Compare hundreds first. If they are equal, compare tens; if those are equal, compare ones. Ascending order goes from smallest to largest, and descending order reverses it.
